html:
In the plebiscite of 5 October 1988, Chileans voted on whether Augusto Pinochet should rule for eight more years. The No side won with about 56 percent of the vote, ending his dictatorship.

The vote was called for by Pinochet's own constitution of 1980. The opposition parties joined forces, registered millions of voters and ran a cheerful television campaign with the slogan "joy is coming". Turnout was very high. On the night, the junta's other members forced Pinochet to accept the result.

Elections followed in 1989, and the Christian Democrat Patricio Aylwin took office in 1990. The transition kept many of Pinochet's rules and left him at the head of the army, but it was one of the most peaceful exits from dictatorship of the time, and the democracy of Chile has held since. It closed the era opened by the coup.
sum: In the plebiscite of 5 October 1988, Chileans voted on whether Augusto Pinochet should rule for eight more years. The No side won with about 56 percent of the vote, ending his dictatorship.
